holes.description: Par 3, 189/169/153 yd, men's 9-hole HCP 5. Golf Top 18's North/South review (last reviewed 2004) describes it as a par three with 'a very wide green that seems to horseshoe around a very deep and unforgiving bunker'. Any shot hit long ends up on a steep hill, pitching to a green that runs severely away from the player. A Greenskeeper.org North 9 tip (Daddy_IRS) agrees: the green is wide but not deep, so a high shot helps it stop; a deep bunker guards the front; from long, the chip or putt is downhill and fast; distance control is essential. WARNING: a search-engine summary wrongly tied a 'hidden lake to the right of the fairway about 80 yards from the green' to this hole. On the Golf Top 18 page that sentence belongs to SOUTH hole 2, not North 2.
holes.elevation: Steep hillside behind the green, so a long miss leaves a downhill chip or putt running fast toward the front. The green tilts away from a player above and behind it, i.e. back-to-front toward the tee.
hazards: very deep front greenside bunker that the green horseshoes (wraps) around
steep bank or hill behind (long) the green
green very wide but shallow (not deep)

north.notes:
I found very little hole-by-hole content for the North nine online. Only North 1 (green size), North 2 and North 3 have explicit descriptions.

WHERE I LOOKED
- The club site (mtngatecc.com and /golf/) has no course tour, hole descriptions, flyovers or scorecard PDF. web.archive.org cannot be fetched from here.
- Greenskeeper.org (index, reviews, scorecard pages). The full tips page (4 tips) needs a login, so only the 2 tips shown on the index page were read.
- Golf Top 18 North/South review.
- bogeysacrossamerica 2015 review. It covers the Lake/North combination but has only a Lake 5 note.
- GolfPass North/South and Lake/North pages. They have only general 'hilly' remarks, and their hole-numbered photo captions refer to Lake holes.
- BlueGolf Lake/North page (says 'No hole description').
- hole19 and 18birdies: star ratings only.
- scgolf, golflink, goprivategolf, wander.golf, mountaingate.la, imgprestige: nothing hole-specific.
- No YouTube flyover or vlog was found.
- Golfify returned 403, Yelp 403, alisterlinks 429.

GENERAL NORTH-NINE CHARACTER (sourced, not hole-specific)
- Golf Top 18: 'The north nine is short, hilly and otherwise forgettable, but difficult due to the small greens and thick rough.' Shots over cliffs and water are attributed to the SOUTH nine, not the North.
- goprivategolf: the North offers challenging terrain with narrow fairways and small greens.
- Greenskeeper JohnnyGK (played North/Lake): a narrow, hilly course with most fairways playing uphill, Kikuyu grass with almost no roll, and small elevated greens guarded by bunkers and Kikuyu rough, with two tiers.
- GolfPass GreerGolf: 'most fairways falling away from the side where the cart path was located.'
- Design credit: Ted Robinson. golflink and goprivategolf also credit Casey O'Callaghan; golflink gives 1976 as the North's opening year.
- USGA/engineering sources: the 27 holes sit on four filled canyons of a former LA County landfill, with methane recovered and piped to UCLA.

CORRECTION
A search-engine summary placed the 'hidden lake to the right of the fairway about 80 yards from the green' on North 2. On the Golf Top 18 page it belongs to SOUTH 2, which winds left around a canyon to a peninsula green. South 3 (canyon short, left and long, with the hidden lake down the hill to the right) and South 4 (bite off the corner to an elevated green) are also described there, which is useful for the South research.

holes.description: Card: Par 4, 400/387/359 yd, SI 1 (hardest hole on the N/S card). GolfTop18 (last reviewed 2004) calls it the best hole on the course. It is a par 4 that winds left around a canyon from tee to green, and the player has to cut off some of the canyon to leave a reasonable approach. The green sits out on a peninsula with bunkers around it and canyon short, left and long. A hidden lake lies right of the fairway about 80 yd from the green, so even a layup has to avoid it. SkyGolf blog (2013) describes a 400-yd par 4: a severe, almost U-shaped dogleg with a ravine to carry on the second shot to a well-protected green. CONFLICT: SkyGolf calls it a dogleg RIGHT. The GolfTop18 text, the OSM hole line (-59 deg turn) and aerial imagery all show it turning LEFT: the tee is at the north, the fairway runs south beside a wooded canyon on the player's left (east), then turns left (east) to the green. Treat it as a dogleg left. SkyGolf photos: from the tee, a brushy ravine and trees are on the left and the fairway is on the right; the approach photo shows the green beyond a brush-filled ravine with three bunkers across its front. The 'hidden lake' matches a triangular pond that OSM does not map. It sits about 80 yd short of the green and about 45-65 yd right of the line, at roughly UTM11N 363397E 3774557N (lon -118.48095, lat 34.10291). A second pond, which OSM does map (way 950199971), lies about 100 yd right, further south. OSM bunkers: 3 greenside (1 left, 2 right) and 1 fairway bunker right about 243 yd.

holes.description: Card: Par 3, 174/153/97 yd, SI 13. GolfTop18 (2004): a par 3 with a nerve-racking approach that puts a premium on accuracy. Canyon lies short, left and long. Right looks safe, but a ball that goes too far right runs down a hill into the hidden lake. The green is relatively flat. SkyGolf blog (2013) has photos taken from the 3rd tee that look down on the I-405 and out to Westwood and the Getty Center, so the tee sits high on the canyon rim. Its photos of the hole show the green across a brush-covered canyon, with bunkers on the front-left and a large tree behind. A GolfNow/GolfPass photo ('hole #3 at South Course') shows the green on a ridge with bunkers on both sides and a drop-off with city views beyond. OSM: the line plays straight SSW. There are 3 greenside bunkers (2 left, 1 right). The OSM-mapped pond (way 950199971) is about 39 yd right of the line near the green (about 163 yd from the tee) and downhill. DEM: tee about 356 m, green about 353 m, canyon floor about 340 m between them.

pond (hidden lake) right of and below the green (GolfTop18; OSM way 950199971)

holes.description: Card: Par 4, 365/356/224 yd, SI 9. The 224-yd forward tee suggests it sits past the pond and the corner. GolfTop18 (2004): a pretty tee shot where the player can cut off more of the corner to leave a shorter, better-angled approach to an elevated green. GolfTop18 does not say which way it bends; the OSM line bends LEFT about 28 deg about 180 yd out. SkyGolf photos (2013): the tee shot crosses native brush and a ravine to a fairway beyond. The green photo shows a large shaped front bunker, the cart path on the left and pampas grass on the right. OSM: the back-tee line crosses the mapped pond (way 950199971) about 39-56 yd from the tee, a short forced carry. Fairway bunkers frame the corner: left about 188 and 234 yd, right about 197 and 222 yd. There is 1 greenside bunker on the right. DEM: green about 3 m above the tee.

holes.description: Card: Par 5, 562/540/481 yd, SI 3, the longest hole on N/S. Older GolfPass and OpenGolfAPI cards list a 412-yd par 4; the 2013 SkyGolf caption, the current card and OSM all say par 5. SkyGolf blog (2013): a 562-yd par 5 with a severe 90-degree dogleg. The side of the hill runs along one side of the fairway and the fairway slopes away on the other. CONFLICT: SkyGolf says dogleg RIGHT with the hill on the right. Its own tee photo shows the brushy hill (houses on top) on the LEFT. OSM (-40 deg on the line; the fairway bends harder) and imagery show the hole turning LEFT, with the hillside and houses on the left/SW. Treat it as a dogleg left. Greenskeeper reviewer roarksown1 (Aug 2016) played South first and then North. While criticising the South nine (sloping fairways, awkward tee angles, lost-ball areas), he complained about finishing a nine on a par 5 where a perfectly struck driver rolls down a hill. That almost certainly means this hole, but he does not number it. SkyGolf approach photo: green with bunkers left and right, buildings (clubhouse area) behind. The photo looking back from the green shows the fairway falling away, so the green sits well above the landing area. DEM: tee about 365 m, dips slightly about 140 yd out, then climbs to the green at about 388 m (+23 m). OSM maps only 2 greenside bunkers (left, right). Imagery shows about 3 fairway bunkers on the outside (right) of the corner and about 2 more on the right of the second leg, none of them in OSM.

south.notes:
I found no hole-by-hole South description from the club itself, Golf Digest (403), BlueGolf (aerial tour only) or YouTube. Only three written sources describe South holes:
(1) GolfTop18 (last reviewed 2004) covers South 2, 3 and 4.
(2) The SkyGolf blog, 13 Aug 2013, has text on South 2 and 9 plus captioned photos of South 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9. The live skygolfblog.com domain now serves unrelated spam, so use the Wayback copy: https://web.archive.org/web/20160826215313/http://www.skygolfblog.com/2013/08/mountaingate-country-club-los-angeles.html
(3) A Greenskeeper review (roarksown1, 13 Aug 2016) gives general South criticism and the finishing par 5.

General South-nine notes:
- SkyGolf: it plays on a plateau at the base of the mountains, is more open and less forgiving than North, and is about 300 yd longer. On clear days downtown LA and Catalina are visible from the highest South tees.
- GolfTop18: shots over cliffs and water.
- Greenskeeper: many sloping fairways, awkward tee angles, lost-ball and penalty areas.

Scorecard check:
- The 6,719-yd card (Golfify, golfingrecord, SkyGolf 2013 captions) has South = 417/400/174/365/535/412/202/450/562, pars 4-4-3-4-5-4-3-4-5, total 3,517.
- OSM pars for refs 19-27 match this card, and OSM hole lengths match within about 15 yd (South 4 is 327 vs 365). That confirms OSM refs 19-27 = South 1-9 = course holes 10-18.
- The GolfPass and OpenGolfAPI N/S scorecard rows (back nine 3,528: 435 / 391 / 302 P4 / 412 P4) are outdated or wrong. Do not use them.

Left/right conflicts:
- SkyGolf calls South 2 and South 9 doglegs RIGHT. The GolfTop18 text (South 2), SkyGolf's own South 9 tee photo, the OSM hole lines and the Esri imagery all show LEFT turns. I used left.

Two OSM gaps worth fixing for metadata (TODO item 3):
(a) The triangular pond about 80 yd short of the South 2 green on the right is not tagged as water in OSM. It is at about UTM11N 363397E 3774557N (lon -118.48095, lat 34.10291) and fits GolfTop18's 'hidden lake'. About 75 m south of it is the OSM-mapped pond (way 950199971, about 1,620 m2). That one lies right of the South 3 green and in front of the South 4 back tee.
(b) On South 9, imagery shows about 5 fairway bunkers on the right of the corner and second leg that OSM does not have.

Method for the derived data (not written sources):
- Everything labelled OSM/DEM or imagery comes from my analysis of research/osm_golf.json, build/backdrop_dem.tif (2 m, approximate) and data/imagery/esri_z20_course.tif.
- Dogleg sign: negative turn = left.
- Per the instructions, holes with no written description (10, 14, 15, 16, 17) are marked 'unknown' even though they carry photo and OSM/DEM observations.

YouTube:

facts.statement: The North/South 18 has exactly ONE open-water feature, a small pond (~1,600 m2, ~200 m perimeter, centroid 34.10228,-118.48082) on the South nine. OSM tags it golf=water_hazard + natural=water (way 950199971). It sits almost directly in front of, and slightly left of, the South #4 tee (GSPro hole 13). It starts within ~40-70 m of the tee, so it is a short forced carry/visual hazard off the tee. It is also ~32-35 m right (west) of the South #3 green (GSPro hole 12, par 3, which plays roughly south). The project's Esri imagery tile (z18 44796_104628, z17 22398_52314) shows dark water ringed by tan bare/native ground, with the South #3 green and its two bunkers just east of it. The OSM-derived opengolfapi listing says '2 water hazards' for North/South. In OSM, though, the second hazard is the Lake-nine pond, not a North or South one.

The North nine has NO open water. OSM has a line tagged waterway=stream (way 1059731972, ~820 m, no name, not marked intermittent). It runs SW to NE from near the North #7/#8 area (34.1091,-118.4918) to the Lake-nine pond (34.1135,-118.4856). It crosses the centrelines of North #1 (~256 yd from tee, near the right side of the green), North #2 (~151 yd from tee on the 189-yd par 3), North #8 (~94 yd from tee) and North #9 (~279 yd from tee), and Lake #1, #8 and #9. It does not cross any OSM fairway, green, tee or bunker polygon. At the crossing points the Esri z19 imagery shows only grass with a faint linear mark and a cart-path crossing, with no water. The line matches the straight ~0.5 m-deep SW-to-NE linear swale already found in the LiDAR (research/NOTES.md). Treat it as a buried storm drain or grassed swale, not a creek. The separate brown 'barranca' right of North #1 green that NOTES.md describes (native/mulch, with a cart bridge) is a dry native area, which may warrant a red penalty-area or native-area surface rather than water.

The Lake nine (scenery only for this build) has the other pond: OSM way 1059732898, golf=water_hazard, ~3,200 m2, centroid ~34.11386,-118.48596. It fronts the Lake #6 green (par 3, ~183 yd) and lies beside Lake #5 and Lake #7. In imagery a cart path or bridge splits it into two lobes. OSM also has minor drain lines near the South #8 green and South #9 tee (ways 345403525, 345403946; 40-70 m long, 50-70 m from play) and intermittent streams well south of the course (>290 m from any South hole). None of these are in play.

Some directory text about water is unreliable. GoPrivateGolf says the Lake course 'features water hazards on every hole'. A search-engine summary attributed to wander.golf mentions an 'island green', but the fetched wander.golf page does not contain that text. Both are contradicted by OSM and imagery, which show only one pond on Lake and one on South. Golf Tennessee and SCGolf list 'Water Hazards: N/A' for North/South.

MountainGate was built over a former municipal solid-waste landfill. The Mountaingate landfill used several canyons in the Brentwood/Sepulveda Pass area, and the LA County Sanitation Districts operated it until 1980. Landfill gas is still recovered there. The USGA Green Section Record of July/Aug 1994 (Vol. 32 No. 4) put Mountaingate CC on its cover as a course 'successfully built on landfill sites'. It reported that ~5 million cu ft/day of methane is piped 5.5 miles to UCLA's steam plant, and that four of the filled canyon surfaces support the 27 holes. EJMap lists a 'Mountaingate Landfill' at 34.1073,-118.4880 (the middle of the course) with a 7.5 MW landfill-gas turbine, and names Barclay Hollander/American Golf Corp. OSM has a disused landfill polygon just south of the South nine (way 345404049) and industrial buildings at ~34.0969,-118.4797 (likely the gas plant). Modelling implications: fill-cap terraces, flat-ish engineered landforms, and possible gas wellheads or vent risers and drainage channels in the rough.

No published golf-course renovation (bunkers, greens, tees, tree removal) since ~2015 was found. Searches of trade press (Golf Course Architecture, GCI, USGA), club pages and directories returned nothing. The only documented recent change is the clubhouse restaurant 'The Gate' and its patio, described as 'newly renovated' (undated). The club Social page describes a large patio with fire pits and panoramic views of the North and Lake courses. GolfPass credits 'Ted Robinson, Sr. and Casey O'Callaghan Golf Course Design' as architects, which may indicate later remodel work, but no details or dates were found. Member reviews mention routine work only: an overseed with cart-path-only play (Oct 2015), Lake #5 fairway repair (Apr 2015), and 'a little bit beat up' uneven tee boxes (Feb 2021).

Imagery the project already has (Esri World Imagery, 2025-07 and 2026-01) shows extensive non-turf ground between and beside holes. It includes tan bare-dirt or mulch native areas (e.g. around the South #3/#4 pond and along North-nine corridors) and dense chaparral/scrub on the slopes. This looks like drought-era turf reduction plus natural hillside. No dated source was found for when the turf was removed. In GSPro these areas likely need a native/waste or 'pinestraw'-type surface rather than rough.

The January 2025 Palisades Fire forced the Mountaingate community to evacuate. ABC7 (11 Jan 2025) reported goats evacuated from Mountaingate as the fire moved toward the 405. The fire's north-east flare-up of 10-11 Jan burned into Mandeville Canyon, which lies west of Kenter Canyon and Mountaingate. No source reports fire damage to the club or course. Post-fire Esri imagery in the project (2025-07-18 and 2026-01-09) shows green turf and intact tree cover, with no visible burn scar on the North/South holes. The project's LiDAR comes from the USGS 'CA_2025LosAngelesPostWildfire' collection, whose name implies it was flown after the fires. Earlier, the October 2019 Getty Fire evacuation zone was bounded by Kenter Canyon, the 405 and Mountaingate; no course damage was reported then either.

Houses rarely line the North/South fairways closely; most homes sit on ridges above the course. Measured from OSM building footprints to the OSM hole centrelines (research/osm_all.json), the houses within 75 m are: South #1 left near the tee (~45 m); South #6 left by the green (48-68 m); North #3 left (~72 m, about 30% of the way down); North #4 around the tee (~67 m); South #9 left along most of the hole (74-86 m, 20 houses within 130 m). No houses lie within 130 m of North #1, #2, #6, #7, #9 or South #2-#5. North #8 and South #3 have one house each, near the tee and beyond 110 m. A 2016 member review: 'a few houses looming overhead, but not bearing down on you'. BlueGolf's North/South local-rules page says 'Local Rules have not been setup', so no published OB or penalty-area definitions exist. OB lines will have to come from the property/parcel boundary, and the OSM golf_course relation 5201230 boundary is coarse. In GSPro, OB should mostly follow the course perimeter and native hillsides, with the closest house-side OB on South #1, South #6 and South #9 (left).

Fairways and rough are kikuyugrass. GolfPass lists Kikuyu for the North/South fairways. A Greenskeeper.org reviewer (07/09/2019) wrote 'The golf course is primarily Kikuyu grass so you got next to no roll with your drives'. Another (07/19/2016) noted 'there was kikuyu in front' of the greens, so short shots got grabbed. An Oct 2015 review mentions overseeding, which suggests winter overseed. Golf Tennessee's directory instead lists Bermuda fairways, which is less credible.

The putting-green species is uncertain. Golf Tennessee lists 'Bent Grass' greens; GolfPass and GoPrivateGolf list Kikuyu greens, which is very unlikely for greens. A 2016 Greenskeeper reviewer said 'same grass and greens as Brookside', and Brookside Pasadena is a typical SoCal poa/bent and kikuyu course. Reviewers describe the greens as fast, firm and hard to hold ('very quick', 2021), small on the North nine (North #1 'very small'), mostly elevated, and with slippery downhill putts. Best modelling assumption: Poa annua/bentgrass greens, fast, with a kikuyu collar and approach.

Bunker sand is bright white to light cream. Esri z19/z20 imagery shows near-white, slightly warm off-white sand (e.g. tiles 20/179161_418484 and 18/44791_104622). Reviewers call it 'quality sand, groomed' (2019) and 'excellent soft sand' (2015). Bunkers range 'from very steep and difficult, to shallow' (2016), and greens are 'well protected by numerous bunkers' (2017). OSM maps 98 bunkers across all 27 holes. Directory copy (BlueGolf) says 'expansive bunkers' and 'deep roughs'.

No authoritative tree-species inventory was found. The evidence: (a) a search-engine summary attributed to wander.golf says the course threads 'narrow fairways through native chaparral and towering eucalyptus groves', but the fetched page lacks that text, so it is unverified; (b) wedding-venue listings mention 'a cluster of birch trees' at the MountainGate Vista ceremony lawn by the clubhouse; (c) project imagery from January 2026 shows some leafless deciduous trees with pale branching (consistent with sycamores) next to dense dark evergreen canopies (pine/oak/eucalyptus type) and chaparral scrub on the slopes; (d) BlueGolf says 'lush stands of trees frame undulating fairways'. The project's existing archetypes (eucalyptus, oak, pine, sycamore, shrub) fit this. Reasonable split: eucalyptus and pines as tall evergreens, coast live oak, sycamores along swales, chaparral shrubs on the hillsides, and a few birch and ornamentals near the clubhouse.

The clubhouse is OSM way 419975852 (building=yes, sport=golf, start_date 1976, LA County height 8.4 m, footprint ~2,200 m2), centroid 34.10822,-118.48792, just SE of the North #1 tee and next to the North #9 green. Cvent gives 1981 as the year built. Aerial imagery (Esri z18 44791_104623, z19 89583_209246) shows an angular, geometric low-rise building of 1-2 storeys with flat or low-slope charcoal/dark-grey roofs, white parapet or fascia edges, terraces and courtyards, and planting beds. A large asphalt car park and tennis courts lie to the south-west. A second golf building (OSM way 419975078, 1976, 5.5 m high, ~960 m2) sits at 34.10873,-118.49015; it is likely the cart barn or maintenance building.

Wedding-venue listings describe the clubhouse as mid-century-modern / Frank Lloyd Wright-inspired. The listed features are a geometric configuration with natural wood and glass, cascading waterfalls with ferns, bougainvillea and birds-of-paradise, and a main dining room with 'a dramatic glass atrium', 'floor-to-ceiling windows that wrap around three sides of the room' and a cherry-wood ceiling. The style wording comes from a search summary attributed to herecomestheguide.com, whose page returned 404 when fetched; the atrium and window details were confirmed on countryclubreceptions.com. Spaces include the Windows Ballroom (~4,965 sq ft), a Garden Terrace and veranda, and the patio with fire pits overlooking the North and Lake courses. For modelling: dark flat roofs, lots of glazing, warm wood or earth-tone facades, and decorative water features around the clubhouse, which are cosmetic and not in play.

Member reviews describe the course as very hilly and narrow, with many fairways playing uphill or sloping away from the cart path, and elevated greens with deep bunkers. The South nine has 'Lots of sloping fairways' and 'awkward angles off the tee' and closes on a par 5 that runs downhill. There are views of the 405, and holes are cart-path-only at times. The three nines 'seem to run into each other' (shared corridors). Robinson's layouts are described as 'links-style' with the terrain 'left completely natural'. The course opened in 1975/76 (North nine 1976 per NOTES.md).

opengolfapi's North/South back-nine card disagrees with golfingrecord. It lists hole 11 as P4 435, hole 16 as P4 302 and hole 18 as P4 412 (total 6,766). golfingrecord has South #2 P4 400, South #7 P3 202 and South #9 P5 562. OSM's South pars (4,4,3,4,5,4,3,4,5) and its hole-line lengths (South #7 ≈ 197 yd, South #9 ≈ 572 yd) support golfingrecord, so the opengolfapi back nine should not be used. In OSM, hole refs 1-9 = North, 10-18 = Lake, 19-27 = South.

The club appears to be operated by American Golf Corp. Its website is served from an AGC multisite host ('mtngatecc-private.agc-multisite.prod.fruition.net', the same platform as AGC's Wood Ranch and El Camino clubs), and EJMap names 'Barclay Hollander/American Golf Corp.' Barclay Hollander was the original developer. Contact: 12445 MountainGate Dr, Los Angeles CA 90049, (310) 476-6215.
